extracted.intended_audience: Users and developers installing, configuring, testing or developing PARI/GP (system administrators, package builders, and advanced users).
extracted.subtask_description: Practical instructions and requirements for configuring, building, installing, testing, and extending PARI/GP on a target system, including debug/profiling builds, kernel selection, readline support, extra packages, documentation and C-linking advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Installation directories / default destinations
rubrics_metrics.description: The gp binary, scripts (gphelp and tex2mail) go to $prefix/bin; the pari library to $prefix/lib and include files to $prefix/include/pari; other system-dependent data go to $prefix/lib/pari. Architecture-independent files go under $share_prefix (defaults to $prefix/share), man pages under $share_prefix/man and other system-independent data under $share_prefix/pari.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may override prefixes via --share-prefix or set --bindir, --libdir, --includedir, --mandir, --datadir, and --sysdatadir directly when running Configure. Architecture-independent documentation, sample GP scripts/C code and extra packages (elldata, galdata) are installed under $share_prefix/pari.

rubrics_metrics.name: Configure-overriding environment variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Configure lets certain environment variables override defaults: CC (C compiler), DLLD (dynamic library linker), LD (static linker).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can run Configure with env CC=cc to try a different compiler. If you insist on using a C++ compiler and encounter problems with g++, try g++ -fpermissive. Use these variables when Compose detects undesirable defaults on your architecture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appending build flags (CFLAGS/CPPFLAGS/LDFLAGS)
rubrics_metrics.description: The contents of the following variables are appended to values computed by Configure: CFLAGS (flags for CC), CPPFLAGS (preprocessor flags for CC), LDFLAGS (flags for LD).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set these environment variables to add extra compiler/preprocessor/linker flags. Note that Configure sometimes parses include files and does not parse CFLAGS for finding includes (see C_INCLUDE_PATH below).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepending search paths (C_INCLUDE_PATH / LIBRARY_PATH)
rubrics_metrics.description: The contents of the following variables are prepended to the values computed by Configure: C_INCLUDE_PATH (directories searched for include files) and LIBRARY_PATH (directories searched for libraries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add -I to CFLAGS is not always enough because Configure may rely on finding and parsing include files; instead use C_INCLUDE_PATH so Configure can locate headers early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disabling inlining or volatile keyword
rubrics_metrics.description: You may disable inlining by adding -DDISABLE_INLINE to CFLAGS, and prevent the use of the volatile keyword with -DDISABLE_VOLATILE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful on platforms or compilers with problematic inline/volatile behavior; set these via CFLAGS before running Configure or make.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debugging and profiling builds
rubrics_metrics.description: Configure -g creates an Oxxx.dbg directory with a special Makefile for building gp and the PARI library suitable for debugging; Configure -pg creates an Oxxx.prf directory suitable for profiling (gprof).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The gp binary built with make all or make gp is optimized. If you ran Configure -g or -pg and want a special-purpose binary, cd to .dbg or .prf and type make gp, or invoke make gp.dbg or make gp.prf from the top-level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiprecision kernel selection (--kernel)
rubrics_metrics.description: The kernel is specified via --kernel=fully_qualified_kernel_name. PARI kernel has two levels: Level 0 (operations on words) and Level 1 (multi-precision integers and reals). Level 0 values: auto, none, or specific assembler micro-kernels (alpha, hppa, hppa64, ia64, ix86, x86_64, m68k, ppc, ppc64, sparcv7, sparcv8_micro, sparcv8_super). Level 1 values: auto, none, or gmp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A fully qualified kernel name is Level0-Level1 (default auto-auto). A name without '-' is an alias meaning name-none, except 'gmp' stands for auto-gmp. Use these to tune performance or portability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readline detection and configuration options
rubrics_metrics.description: Configure does not aggressively search for the readline library and headers; if they are not in standard places it will not find them. Options: --with-readline[=prefix], --with-readline-lib=path_to_libreadline.xx, --with-readline-include=path_to_readline.h.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On Linux you typically need both readline and readline-devel packages; missing readline-devel or libncurses.so will make Configure complain. On OS X the system provides a fake readline insufficient for gp; consult PARI FAQ for step-by-step OSX readline installation. Use explicit --with-readline-lib/include when libraries/headers are in non-standard paths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Known readline-related problems on Linux and OS X
rubrics_metrics.description: Linux distributions often split readline and readline-devel; both are required. Some distributions incorrectly make readline-devel optional relative to ncurses-devel. On OS X 10.4+ the fake readline causes gp to be built without readline support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Install both packages (readline + readline-devel) and ncurses-devel if needed. For OS X follow PARI FAQ instructions linked from pari.math.u-bordeaux.fr for installing a usable readline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing: diagnosing 'BUG' in make bench (known problems)
rubrics_metrics.description: If BUG appears in make bench: you may have an older installed dynamic PARI library (libpari.so.xxx) producing 'libpari.so.xxx has older revision than expected xxx' or other errors; this indicates a broken local configuration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove the old library or unset LD_LIBRARY_PATH. Unset or disable LD_LIBRARY_PATH if gp-dyn gives severe errors (e.g., Illegal Instruction). Note gp-sta (static) is unaffected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing: false positives due to diff implementations
rubrics_metrics.description: Some implementations of diff (HPUX etc.) output 'No differences encountered' instead of empty input, which causes spurious [BUG] messages in the tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you see spurious BUG messages, consider that the diff implementation may be non-standard; consult platform-specific notes or use a different diff implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional tests: test-compat and test-ploth
rubrics_metrics.description: Use make test-compat to run gp in compatibility mode. Use make test-ploth to test graphic routines; you must click after each image — there are eight images, probably shown twice (try resizing at least one).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: make bench, make test-compat and make test-ploth produce pari.ps in Oxxx which can be printed to compare Postscript output with screen images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heavy-duty and developer tests
rubrics_metrics.description: make test-kernel checks low-level kernel functionality (useful if make bench fails badly). make test-all runs all available test suites (thorough but slow) and may require extra packages (elldata, galdata). To test extra packages before installing, run env GP_DATA_DIR=$PWD/data make test-all from PARI toplevel. make test-io tests I/O and requires working system(). make test-time checks timers and may fail on heavy load or low timer granularity. make test-install tests install/GP function install and may not be available on some platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use make test-kernel only when needed; for make test-all ensure extra packages are available or set GP_DATA_DIR to local data to avoid installing prematurely. Retry make test-time a few times before reporting bugs due to timer granularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: make install usage and umask caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: When ready to install, run make install (may require superuser privileges — e.g., sudo make install on Mac OS X). It is advised to run make all first to avoid running unnecessary commands as root. Install directories are created honoring your umask; a too-restrictive umask (e.g., 077) will create installed files not world-readable. Running sudo may change your user umask.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run make all before make install when using root/sudo. Check and adjust umask so installed files have correct permissions; if using sudo be aware that umask may be altered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Static vs dynamic binaries and libraries (tradeoffs)
rubrics_metrics.description: By default, if a dynamic libpari.so can be built, the installed gp binary is gp-dyn linking to libpari.so. You can build a statically linked gp (libpari.a) which is machine-specific. The static library libpari.a is not created by default; use make install-lib-sta to create it and make install-bin-sta to install a statically linked gp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Static binaries may be slightly faster (~5%, possibly up to 20% with pthreads), use more disk space, and take longer to compile. Statically linked programs are harder to upgrade (must recompile rather than updating the shared library) but are immune to breakage from installing a new PARI library.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extra optional packages and their purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional packages: elldata (elliptic curves from Cremona's database; needed by ellidentify, ellsearch, forell and useful for ellinit), galdata (allows Galois groups >7 and <11), seadata (database of modular polynomials used to speed ellap, ellcard, ellgroup for large primes), galpol (GALPOL database of polynomials for galoisgetpol).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To install a package pack: download pack.tgz from the PARI server, copy the archive into PARI toplevel directory, extract so contents go to data/pack/, then typing make install installs all such packages.

rubrics_metrics.name: GPRC file setup and customization
rubrics_metrics.description: Copy misc/gprc.dft (or gprc.dos for GP.EXE) to $HOME/.gprc and modify it (e.g., remove control characters from prompt if not using an ANSI terminal, enable colors). You can read $datadir/misc/gpalias from gprc for common shortcuts and fix paths accordingly. For system-wide defaults copy customized .gprc to /etc/gprc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If gp complains it cannot find gphelp, check .gprc (or system-wide gprc) for explicit paths and correct them according to misc/gprc.dft. Unless datadir was altered via Configure, datadir is $prefix/share/pari.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation build and PDF generation
rubrics_metrics.description: make all builds documentation; alternatively type make doc. A working plain TeX installation is required. DVI files produced include libpari.dvi, users.dvi, tutorial.dvi and refcard.dvi. If pdftex is present, type make docpdf to produce PDF (with hyperlinks). The reference card is also available as PostScript, landscape A4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can gzip usersch*.tex and dvi files to save disk space; the online-help system handles compressed files. Built documents are available online from the PARI home page.

rubrics_metrics.name: C programming and linking to PARI
rubrics_metrics.description: Once libraries and include files are installed, you can link C programs to the PARI library. A sample examples/Makefile illustrates library usage. make all in examples builds extgcd-sta (statically linked), extgcd-dyn (dynamically linked), and shared libextgcd usable from gp via install.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standalone (statically linked) binary is usually robust; dynamically linked binaries or shared libraries may fail if runtime library paths are wrong. If extgcd-dyn reports 'DLL not found', either use static linking or consult system docs about setting link paths. On Windows, ensure libpari.dll is in PATH.

rubrics_metrics.name: GP sample scripts and examples location
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete sample GP programs are provided in the examples directory (SQUFOF, Pollard rho, Lucas-Lehmer, class group/unit algorithms). See examples/EXPLAIN for explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review these samples to learn idiomatic GP scripting and to test functionality on your build.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bug reporting procedure and community resources
rubrics_metrics.description: PARI home page maintains mailing lists, documentation, downloads and a Bug Tracking System (BTS). Bug reports should be submitted to the BTS. For configuration problems include the relevant *.dif files in the Oxxx directory and the file pari.cfg when reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer submitting bugs to the BTS (link provided) but use pari-dev or pari-users mailing lists for discussion. Mailing lists: pari-announce (read-only), pari-dev (development, patches, discussion), pari-users (general questions). Subscribe by sending a request message with 'subscribe' in Subject to the listed request addresses. General inquiries can be emailed to pari@math.u-bordeaux.fr but individual replies are not guaranteed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation format for PARI in publications
rubrics_metrics.description: If you used PARI in a paper, cite it in the provided BibTeX/manual format (example given in the manual with organization, title = '{PARI/GP version 2.9.5}', year = 2017, address = 'Bordeaux', note = 'available from \url{http://pari.math.u-bordeaux.fr/}').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the exact BibTeX template provided in the manual so credit/citation is consistent across publications.
